title: Finite polynomial curve images and complete admitted two-helper overlap closure

newly_cached_primary_context.title: On images of affine spaces
newly_cached_primary_context.author: Ivan Arzhantsev
newly_cached_primary_context.portions_inspected: Section 1 through Lemma 1: Definition 1 and scalar-unit observation, Example 2 omitting the origin, Lemma 1(c) on curve images; later flexibility statements were not used.
newly_cached_primary_context.role: Primary context for polynomial curve images and the surface omission boundary. The needed surjectivity is proved directly by restricting to a line and making its parameter integral over the curve algebra; the scalar-unit fact and omitted-origin example are also verified directly. No curve-normalization or flexibility classification is imported.

retained_structural_imports.statement: Retained miracle-flatness theorem for Noetherian local rings with regular base, Cohen-Macaulay source and dimension equality.
retained_structural_imports.role: New application to the geometric generic helper plane. Expected dimensions of all nonempty fibres are proved; empty fibres are allowed, so global faithfulness is not assumed.

direct_proof_arguments: a dominant polynomial map from affine space to an affine curve restricts to a finite surjective line map because its parameter is integral over one nonconstant coordinate polynomial
dominance injects curve functions into a polynomial source algebra and makes every curve unit scalar
a multiplier-zero source component fixes its row; full parameter action and within-row transitivity make it target-fixed and force source-field degree one
in two helper variables the common positive-coefficient drop locus is finite over the parameter closure and its generic target fibres are empty
every other generic forgetful fibre has the expected pure dimension, giving flatness by the retained miracle-flatness theorem without global faithfulness
flat pullback to each helper curve injects its ring into the polynomial generic fibre, excluding hidden divisors and nilpotents
actual source affine-space components surject onto their helper curves; their disjointness makes those curves disjoint with scalar units
ordinary degree in the helper polynomial plane gives a descended common pencil whose outer degree is exactly the original source-field degree
rank-two global helper linearization forces that degree one, closing all admitted two-helper overlaps in every stable dimension and the complete admitted HC4 overlap family
